unit_notes.price: BIS Residential Property Prices for GREECE, NATIONWIDE, NOMINAL, index 2010=100 (FRED mirror id QGRN628BIS; underlying source BIS selected residential property price series). Quarterly level, not seasonally adjusted. Full coverage 1997Q1-2026Q1, 117/117, no gaps. CHOICE OF SERIES: the Bank of Greece 'Index of Apartment Prices by Geographical Area: Athens' (BoG Open Data dataset 5, base 2007=100) is the city-granular alternative but starts only 2006Q1 (81 quarters). The compass measures cycle position, for which 117 quarters of history beats city granularity, so the BIS national series was used. The two agree on shape (BoG Athens: nominal peak 2008Q2, trough 2017Q1, -44.7%, then +107.5%; BIS national: peak 2008Q3, trough 2017Q3, -42.4%, then +90.0%). NOT SPLICED with the BoG pre-2006 annual Athens series: there is a documented definitional break at 2005/06 and splicing across it would be invented data. Real (CPI-deflated) counterpart is QGRR628BIS. NOTE the BoG series flags 2025Q2-2026Q1 as Provisional and revises them; BIS does not publish a status flag, so the BIS tail should be treated as equally provisional. fred.stlouisfed.org/series/QGRN628BIS
unit_notes.pti: NOT SOURCED -- all 117 null. No official Greek price-to-income ratio exists. Greece is absent from Eurostat's house price index collection entirely (prc_hpi_q returns zero observations for geo=EL, so there is also no independent cross-check on the BIS price series), and no OECD analytical price-to-income indicator for Greece is carried on FRED (five candidate ids probed, all 404). Valuation must fall back to price/income downstream -- see the `income` note; that fallback has a denominator only from 1999Q1.
unit_notes.months: SUPPLY FLOW, NOT MONTHS-OF-INVENTORY. Eurostat sts_cobp_q (Building permits by type of building, quarterly), indic_bt=BPRM_DW (number of dwellings authorised), cpa2_1=CPA_F41001_X_410014 (residential buildings excluding residences for communities), s_adj=NSA, unit=I21 -> INDEX, 2021=100. Quarterly, 1995Q1-2026Q1 at source; 117/117 on this axis, no gaps. Same slot and same sign convention as `months` in au_raw.json (ABS building approvals): HIGH = more permits = LOOSE future supply; the engine applies sign -1 so low = tight = +. NOT SEASONALLY ADJUSTED: median NSA/SCA factors are Q1 0.881, Q2 1.018, Q3 0.993, Q4 1.114, i.e. a +-12% seasonal on a series whose range is 32x (20.3 in 2016Q1 to 1505.0 in 2005Q4), so seasonality is small relative to signal. A seasonally-and-calendar-adjusted variant (s_adj=SCA) exists but only from 2000Q1 and was rejected for costing 12 quarters of history. CONVERSION: the index x 22.6/100 = thousands of dwellings authorised per year at an annual average, i.e. one index point = 56.5 dwellings in a quarter; annual averages reproduce Eurostat's published dwelling counts to +-0.2k (2005 174.2k vs 174.4k published; 2015 5.5k; 2021 22.6k; 2024 41.7k; 2025 31.9k). 2005Q4 = 1505.0 is a genuine regulatory pull-forward (19% VAT on new buildings applied to permits issued from 1 Jan 2006), not an error. 2025 is depressed by a second regulatory artefact -- the New Building Regulation (NOK) floor-area/height bonuses were suspended nationwide in Dec 2024 and only clarified in May 2025 -- so the 2026Q1 +70.2% y/y is off an artificially weak base and is NOT a clean demand signal. DEFINITIONAL CONFLICT to carry: ELSTAT's own Building Activity Survey reports 39,219 dwellings authorised in 2025 against Eurostat's 31.9k, because ELSTAT counts total new dwellings across all building activity while Eurostat excludes residences for communities. Both are tier 1; do not average them.
unit_notes.vacancy: NOT SOURCED -- all 117 null. Greece has no quarterly, annual or even regularly-repeating vacancy series. The only tier-1 vacancy observations are the 2011 and 2021 population-and-housing censuses (ELSTAT), i.e. two points ten years apart, which cannot be put on a quarterly axis without inventing 38 values between them. Eurostat has no cens_21dwe / cens_21dwoc for Greece (404). FOR THE RECORD, and for use in prose rather than in this array: the widely-quoted '2.2 million vacant homes = 34.5%' is the BROAD definition and sweeps in island and rural holiday homes; the NARROW 2021 figure, excluding secondary/holiday residences, is 793,884 nationally (Attica 255,298), of which for rent 406,859, for sale 59,530, closed for other reasons 327,495. Municipality of Athens: 437,188 dwellings, 117,137 vacant on the broad definition. THE SUPPLY AXIS IS STILL LIVE for Greece because `months` is fully populated -- unlike Thailand, build_compass will NOT emit supply_available=false here. It rests on one component (permits), not two.
unit_notes.pop: Eurostat namq_10_pe (Employment and population by A*10 industry breakdowns, quarterly national accounts), na_item=POP_NC (total population, national concept), unit=THS_PER, s_adj=NSA. THOUSANDS OF PERSONS. Quarterly, 1995Q1-2026Q1 at source; 117/117 on this axis, no gaps, and NOT a step function -- unlike Thailand's `pop`, quarter-on-quarter change is non-zero throughout, so build_compass's special handling for annual-stepped population is NOT needed here. CAVEAT: this is a national-accounts population, compiled by interpolating annual demographic statistics onto quarters; within-year movement is the compiler's interpolation, not an independent quarterly observation. Quarter-on-quarter changes are therefore smooth by construction and only year-on-year change carries real information. It reconciles with the World Bank series (POPTOTGRA647NWDB) exactly to 2020 (1997 10,661.2 vs 10,661.3; 2010 11,121.4 vs 11,121.3) but runs 70-126 thousand above it from 2021, because the national-accounts concept absorbed the 2021 census differently from WDI -- the two differ in level after 2021 but agree on direction. Peak 2010Q4 = 11,122.9k; 2026Q1 = 10,549.2k, -5.16% from peak. No census step is visible in the series.
unit_notes.credit: BIS credit to households and NPISHs, GREECE, ALL LENDERS, ALL PURPOSES -- a LEVEL in BILLIONS OF EUROS, adjusted for breaks (FRED mirror id CRDQGRAHABIS). Quarterly, 1994Q4-2025Q4 at source; 116/117 on this axis. 2026Q1 is null because BIS credit lags BIS prices by one quarter. THIS IS A LEVEL, NOT A RATIO: the %-of-GDP twin QGRHAM770A exists on FRED and using it here would corrupt the money axis, because the engine deflates `credit` by `cpi` and takes real growth. Verified: credit / trailing-4Q gdp reproduces the published QGRHAM770A to 0.05pp at five checkpoints (2025Q4 calc 38.05% vs published 38.1%). Peak EUR 139.3bn 2010Q3 -> EUR 94.3bn 2025Q4 = -32.3%, and the level has been FLAT-TO-RISING since 2022 (91.8 -> 94.3bn) while the ratio kept falling, i.e. recent 'deleveraging' is denominator growth. DO NOT CONFUSE with the ECB MFI bank balance-sheet housing-loan stock (M.GR.N.A.A22.A.1.U6.2250.Z01.E), which fell EUR 80.3bn (Aug 2010) to EUR 25.2bn (Jun 2026) = -68.6%: that series is bank-held mortgages only, and the gap between -68.6% and -32.3% is the Hercules/HAPS securitisations moving loans off bank books to servicers and SPVs -- the households still owe them. This field deliberately carries the all-lender measure so that transfer does not appear as repayment. fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CRDQGRAHABIS
unit_notes.rate: POLICY RATE, PERIOD AVERAGE, PERCENT. *** SPLICED at 2000Q4/2001Q1 *** because Greece adopted the euro on 1 January 2001 and has had no national policy rate since. LEG 1, 1997Q1-2000Q4: drachma-era overnight interbank / call money rate, OECD via FRED IRSTCI01GRM156N, monthly, converted to quarterly by simple average of the three months (no month missing). This is a MARKET rate, not a policy target; the 1997Q4 = 17.219% print is the genuine October 1997 defence of the drachma, not an error. LEG 2, 2001Q1-2026Q1: ECB DEPOSIT FACILITY RATE (FRED ECBDFR), calendar-daily, converted to quarterly by simple average of all days in the quarter (series is daily with zero missing days, 1999-01-01 to 2026-07-31). WHY THE DFR AND NOT THE MAIN REFINANCING RATE: (a) FRED's ECBMRRFR is NULL from 2000-06-28 to 2008-10-14 -- the variable-rate-tender era, when the minimum bid rate rather than a fixed rate applied -- so it covers only 74 of the 117 quarters and would need a second splice; (b) since 18 September 2024 the DFR is the rate through which the ECB explicitly steers the stance; (c) the DFR is the only one of the three key rates that registers the negative-rate easing, going negative in 34 quarters (2014Q2-2022Q3, minimum -0.50%), whereas the MRO sat at exactly 0.00% throughout and would have made the rate component of the money axis identically flat across the entire Greek housing recovery. Current values for reference: DFR 2.00% in 2026Q1, raised to 2.25% on 17 June 2026; MRO 2.40% at end-July 2026. SPLICE STEP: 2000Q4 7.177% -> 2001Q1 3.750% = -3.427pp. That decomposes into -2.333pp of genuine convergence (the same OECD call-money concept fell 7.177% -> 4.843% across the same join as Greek overnight rates snapped to euro-area levels) and -1.093pp of concept change (overnight market rate vs the floor of the ECB corridor, then ~100bp wide). Year-on-year change across 2001Q1-2001Q4 is therefore NOT clean and should not be read as monetary easing of that size.
unit_notes.cpi: INDEX LEVEL, NOT AN INFLATION RATE. Eurostat Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices, all items, Greece (FRED mirror id CP0000GRM086NEST), monthly, base 2025=100 (verified: 2025 monthly average = 100.002; the series is identical in shape to the Eurostat 2015=100 publication, constant ratio 0.81464). MONTHLY -> QUARTERLY BY SIMPLE AVERAGE OF THE THREE MONTHS; every quarter on the axis has all three months, so no quarter is a partial average. Source coverage 1996-01 to 2026-06; 117/117 on this axis, no gaps. NOT SEASONALLY ADJUSTED (Greek HICP has a large January/February sales effect), so quarter-on-quarter change is seasonal and only year-on-year change should be used. The deflation is real and visible: rebased to 2010=100 the index reads 2012 104.18, 2013 103.29, 2014 101.85, 2015 100.74, 2016 100.76, 2020 101.92, 2021 102.51 -- the whole 2010-2021 decade produced about 2.5% cumulative inflation -- then 2022 112.04 and 2025 123.66. ALTERNATIVE CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: the OECD/national Greek CPI (FRED GRCCPIALLMINMEI, 2015=100) is EXACTLY the deflator BIS uses -- price/that CPI reproduces the published BIS real index QGRR628BIS with a worst residual of 0.045% across all 113 overlapping quarters -- but it is discontinued at 2025-04, so it cannot cover 2025Q2-2026Q1 and cannot be refreshed. Using it would have required splicing at the most recent and most-read end of the series. The cost of using HICP instead is a maximum level divergence of 2.15% from BIS's own deflator over 29 years (about 0.07pp a year), which is immaterial for real growth rates. fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CP0000GRM086NEST
unit_notes.gdp: Eurostat quarterly national accounts, gross domestic product at market prices, CURRENT PRICES, MILLIONS OF EUROS, seasonally and calendar adjusted (FRED mirror id CPMNACSCAB1GQEL; Eurostat namq_10_gdp, na_item=B1GQ, unit=CP_MEUR, s_adj=SCA). Quarterly level, 1995Q1-2026Q1 at source; 117/117 on this axis, no gaps. This is a NOMINAL level, matching the units of `credit` (EUR bn -- note the 1000x unit difference) and `income` (EUR mn). Annual sums: 1997 EUR 111.0bn, 2008 EUR 238.7bn (pre-crisis peak), 2013 EUR 178.2bn, 2020 EUR 168.0bn, 2025 EUR 247.9bn. Greek REAL GDP is still about 13.8% below its 2008 peak; that fact is not visible in this nominal series and must not be inferred from it. fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPMNACSCAB1GQEL
unit_notes.unemp: Harmonised unemployment rate, all persons, PERCENT, SEASONALLY ADJUSTED, quarterly as published by OECD/Eurostat (FRED mirror id LRHUTTTTGRQ156S). 1998Q2-2026Q1 at source; 112/117 on this axis -- 1997Q1-1998Q1 are null because the harmonised series begins 1998Q2, not because of a fetch failure. No interior gaps. Verified: quarterly peak 2013Q3 = 28.03% and the 2013 four-quarter average = 27.80%, matching the published annual peak of 27.8%. Latest actual 2026Q1 = 9.633% -- note this is the quarterly average of a volatile monthly series (Jan 8.9, Feb 9.9, Mar 10.1) and the monthly series has since printed 8.1% for May 2026, the lowest since 2008; do not quote 9.633% as 'the current unemployment rate'. A longer annual series (LRUN74TTGRA156N, 1961-2025) exists but 1962-1976 are published as 0.0, which is a placeholder and not data. fred.stlouisfed.org/series/LRHUTTTTGRQ156S
unit_notes.income: HOUSEHOLD GROSS DISPOSABLE INCOME, LEVEL, MILLIONS OF EUROS, current prices, seasonally and calendar adjusted. Eurostat nasq_10_nf_tr (quarterly non-financial sector accounts), na_item=B6G, sector=S14_S15 (households and NPISH), direct=PAID, unit=CP_MEUR, s_adj=SCA. Quarterly, 1999Q1-2026Q1 at source; 109/117 on this axis -- 1997Q1-1998Q4 are null because Greek quarterly sector accounts begin 1999Q1. No interior gaps. This is a genuine household-aggregate income level and IS unit-comparable in concept with the `income` field in au_raw.json (ABS household gross disposable income), unlike Thailand's per-worker wage. Not per capita: divide by `pop` if a per-head measure is wanted. Post-crisis trough 2014Q1 EUR 28,199m -> 2026Q1 EUR 41,823m = +48.3% (+51.7% per capita on this file's own `pop`), against BIS nominal prices +90.0% from their 2017Q3 trough. That reproduces the IMF's May 2026 Article IV finding of roughly +85% prices vs +47% disposable income per capita, and is the file's independent corroboration of the valuation story. CONSEQUENCE: with `pti` null, valuation falls back to price/income, which does not exist before 1999Q1; with a 24-quarter standardisation window the first trustworthy valuation z-score is no earlier than about 2005Q1.
